title: Multi-metric stability orchestrator for cohort rollouts
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Build an orchestration layer that observes multiple evaluation signals during canary and A/B cohort rollouts and performs automatic safe-rollbacks when joint statistical thresholds indicate a regression. The feature focuses on combining quality evals (prompt-based metrics, BLEU/ROUGE-style proxies for structured outputs, hallucination counters), latency and error-rate SLOs, and per-customer cost delta. Non-goals: replacing manual canary decisions entirely for high-risk enterprise customers and changing model weights; this layer controls routing/config flips only.
success_criteria: Detect regressions in canaries with >=90% precision at alerting time (<=10% false positives) as measured on historical A/B replays
Auto-rollback within configured SLO window (default 5 minutes) for cohort size >=1% traffic when multi-signal threshold exceeded
Provide explainable provenance in the Console for every automated rollback (metrics, samples, trigger rule) and an opt-out toggle for enterprise clusters
Reduce manual rollback incidence by 60% in the next quarter on internal canaries
acceptance_criteria: Unit + integration tests covering signal aggregation and decision paths
E2E test using replay dataset that injects synthetic regressions and validates rollback occurs
Monitoring dashboard with per-cohort time series for all signals and a recorded event for each automated rollback
Design doc / runbook and on-call alerting with clear remediation steps
design_notes: Signal consolidation: use weighted z-score aggregation across independent metrics (quality, latency, error-rate, cost) with configurable weights per project
Statistical test: sequential probability ratio test (SPRT) for early detection with a configurable alpha/beta; fallback to bootstrap if metric distributions are non-normal
Decision policy: require at least two independent signal families (one must be quality) to exceed thresholds before auto-rollback to reduce false positives
Data pipeline: use the existing eval-ingest topic for sample-level labels and the realtime metrics stream for SLOs; persist aggregated snapshots for provenance
Rollout mechanism: leverage routing policies to move traffic off the candidate model to the previous stable variant and mark cohort as quarantined
implementation_steps: 1) Spec: finalize weighting defaults and risk profiles (PM + Applied ML) - 1 week
2) API: add RolloutGuard config schema to the rollout API (route-level config) - 3 days
3) Aggregator: implement a streaming aggregator that computes z-scores and SPRT outcomes - 2 sprints
4) Decision Engine: implement policy engine with pluggable rules and audit events - 1 sprint
5) Console: render per-cohort signal dashboard, diff view and rollback action modal - 2 sprints
6) E2E Tests: build replay harness and synthetic-regression scenarios - 1 sprint
7) Staged rollout: enable in internal orgs -> beta customers -> GA with opt-out for Dedicated customers
tradeoffs: Conservative multi-signal requirement reduces false positives but increases detection latency for single strong-signal regressions
SPRT provides low-latency detection but assumes IID samples; we mitigate with bootstrap fallback and per-customer calibration
Storing samples for provenance increases storage and PII surface; retention defaults to 30 days and we provide hashing/obfuscation options
risks: False positives causing unnecessary rollbacks and customer trust erosion
Undetected correlated regressions that only show up in long-tail prompts beyond canary size
Operational complexity: more alert noise if thresholds are not tuned per workload
decisions: Use weighted z-score + SPRT hybrid for detection (approved by Applied ML)
Require at least two signal families to trigger auto-rollback, with quality as a mandatory signal family
Expose per-org risk profile (aggressive / balanced / conservative) to tune weights and thresholds
